# PR #1729: Patch: a ruling's proof must be a test that can run

Closes #1718

`cargo jackioh spec check` now credits a `proven_in` file only with a test that can run. Skipped TypeScript tests and plain, unmarked Rust functions no longer count. It reports 1106 rulings and 2539 proofs, `ok` on the real tree, the same count as before. No existing proof turned out to be non-executable, so no `proven_in` entry changed.

## What changed

- **Rust:** a proof is a `fn` with the `r<n>` token that is marked `#[test]`, or any path ending in `::test` such as `#[tokio::test]`. A `#[ignore]` disqualifies it unless the reason starts with `daily:`. A `mod` counts only if its body holds such a test.
- **TypeScript:** a title under `.skip`, `.todo`, `.fixme` or `.only` no longer counts, and neither does anything inside such a call. `.concurrent` and `.each` still count.
- **SQL:** unchanged.
- **Files:** the code is in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` and the wording in `spec/README.md` and `crates/tools/README.md`. The failure message for a missing proof now says "no test that runs".
- **No new ruling.** This is tooling, and rule 3 already says "the proving test".

I followed the planner's code with no departures.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`: 384, 16, 1 and 4 tests pass in its four test binaries, 4 ignored.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh spec::`: 20 pass, including the six the plan named. The `it.skip` fixture and the plain-`fn` fixture now flip to "no proof".
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh catalog check` and `cargo jackioh patches check` are clean.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` prints `Internal`, so no patch fragment is needed.
- I did not run the workspace `cargo test` or workspace clippy: only `crates/tools` and two READMEs changed, so the harness's run will be the first of those.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **A `mod` counts when its body holds a runnable test.** The issue says "a `mod` inside `#[cfg(test)]`". I rejected that because it would fail mods in `tests/` files, which carry no `cfg`, and would credit an empty `mod`.
- **A name listed in a same-file test macro's call counts.** `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` makes its tests with a `both_stores!` macro. Without this rule 61 of its proofs fail even though those tests run. I rejected failing them or rewriting that file.
- **`.only` does not count**, as the issue says, because vitest refuses it under CI.
- **A TypeScript title inside a comment still counts.** The issue names modifiers only, so blanking comments is left for a follow-up.

## For the reviewer

- **`ts_call_end` is a heuristic.** It skips strings and comments but not regex literals or JSX text. An unbalanced quote inside a skipped call can only hide more titles, so the check fails; it never passes a bad proof. No skipped call exists on the tree today.
- **Two kinds of tests that never run still count.** One is a test inside a `macro_rules!` that is never called, the other is a test under a disabled `#[cfg]`. The tree has no case of either.

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 1 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs:780`: `ts_call_end` does not recognise regex literals, so a `)` inside one (`/\)/`) ends a skipped `describe.skip(…)` early, and the titles after it in that group are credited again.
- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs:709`: A vitest options object that skips a test (`it("R8 …", { skip: true }, …)`) still counts as a proof.
- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs:508`: A `#[test]` that is compiled out (`#[cfg(any())]`, or any `cfg` that is false) still counts as a test that runs.

## Risks

- **False failures on the tree.** The prototype gave the same `fn`/`mod` names and lines as today on all 1,469 `.rs` files under `crates/`. So rule 3 is unchanged and 0 proofs flip. If the builder's version flips any, it has diverged from the code above.
- **`rust_code_only` must keep char indices.** Otherwise step 3 reads the wrong `ignore` reason from `source`.
- **`ts_call_end` is a heuristic**, with no awareness of regex literals or JSX text. An unbalanced quote inside a skipped call can only hide more titles. That makes the check fail; it never passes a bad proof. No skipped call exists on the tree today.
- **Two kinds of tests that never run still count:** a test inside a `macro_rules!` that is never called, and one under a disabled `#[cfg]`. That is out of scope, and the tree has no case of either.

## Open questions

None of these block the build. Each was decided here, and a person may overrule it:
- **A `mod` counts when its body holds a test that runs.** The rejected alternative was "any `mod` inside `#[cfg(test)]`". That rule would wrongly fail mods in `tests/` files, which carry no `cfg`, and it would credit an empty mod.
- **Names listed in a same-file test macro's call count.** The rejected alternatives were failing the 61 `contract.rs` proofs or rewriting that file. Those cases do run, as `memory::<case>`.
- **`.only` does not count**, following the issue, because vitest refuses it under CI.
- **A TypeScript title inside a comment still counts.** The issue names modifiers only, so blanking TypeScript comments is left for a follow-up.
- **No new ruling and no `CLAUDE.md` edit.** Rule 3 there already says "the proving test".
